chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mada'ini from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The teacher does not teach for a fixed salary (wage) and he accepts the gift if it is presented to him."

key_terms.إِذَا أُهْدِيَ إِلَيْهِ: If it is presented/offered to him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a teacher receiving a fixed salary versus gifts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia scholarly preference for voluntary knowledge transmission over commercialized teaching, distinguishing between a fixed wage (*ajr*) and accepted gifts (*hadiyyah*). It reflects the broader ethical framework where scholars view their role as a trust (*amanah*) rather than a trade, encouraging generosity from students while maintaining financial independence from rigid salaries. This practice underscores the spiritual value of teaching as an act of worship and community service rather than a mere profession.
